title: Training Ultra Long Context Language Model with Fully Pipelined Distributed Transformer
problem: Training LLMs on extremely long sequences (1M+ tokens) requires memory far exceeding GPU capacity; existing Ulysses-style sequence parallelism is bottlenecked by PCIe transfer latency when offloading to host memory.
motivation: Long-context training (protein sequences, documents) demands sequence parallelism beyond NVLink bandwidth; CPU offloading is necessary but naive implementations serialize compute and transfer, wasting GPU cycles.
method: Fully Pipelined Distributed Transformer (FPDT) extends DeepSpeed Ulysses with CPU memory offloading using a double-buffer design. The sequence is sliced into chunks (default 64K tokens). A pipeline overlaps PCIe host-to-device prefetch of the next chunk with GPU computation on the current chunk. A rank-ordinal scatter redistributes activations across GPUs. The vocabulary computation is also pipelined within the sequence chunk pipeline.
key_novelty: Double-buffer design that hides PCIe latency behind computation, enabling 16x longer sequences than state-of-the-art on the same hardware while maintaining >55% MFU. First system to train 8B LLM with 2M sequence length on only 4 GPUs.
contributions: Sequence chunk pipeline design slicing the full sequence into 64K-token chunks for pipeline execution
Double-buffer prefetching overlapping PCIe host-to-device with GPU compute
Rank-ordinal scatter for efficient cross-GPU activation redistribution
16x increase in trainable sequence length versus prior SOTA on same hardware
Training 8B LLM at 2M sequence length on 4 GPUs with >55% MFU
Compatibility with existing training frameworks (GPT, Llama models)

metrics.sequence_length_improvement: 16x over prior SOTA on same hardware

limitations: MFU of 55% implies 45% overhead from communication/memory transfers; requires sufficient CPU DRAM; chunk size tuning affects both MFU and throughput; does not address gradient checkpointing interaction explicitly.
